item.content:encoded:
Edit: before you read this, please keep in mind that I have a headache. In retrospect, my comment had nothing to do with Decibelles because I mixed up SCP-109 with SCP-402, however what I said in the rant still stands for the most part.

I also don't really like the mention of 109 402 either for two reasons; one, how on earth do they get the clearance to take 109 402 out of containment to use it to remove flooding, and two, it doesn't even remove water, it just makes it so that it can't be perceived. So while you're thinking "I'm glad I used this to get rid of all that water. That sure made my job easy." You're drowning in "nonexistent" water because your body isn't closing your airway to prevent water getting in your lungs. Other than that rant, I like it. +1

item.content:encoded: This is one that's just ok in my mind. Nothing really hooking me, but I'm not turned away by it either. Seems like an odd object, some useful and dangerous with some very clear sets of how it functions. Wish there was some more to it though, otherwise it's just ok to me. On the other hand, for every "Woah-crazy-keter-powered-death-to-11!" scip out there, there really should be some that are just, well, safe enough.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: One way to explore the cryptoriver to which the boxcar gives access might be to use a tethered ROV with an inertial locator on board. This wouldn't help establish the river's location directly, but it would give clear views of the surrounding rock, which might help narrow it down. And of course the layout could also help that way; if fish live in such rivers, that's another potential clue. If the ROV is tethered, and remember that the tether spools can be over a mile long quite easily, you don't even have to worry about losing it.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
whoa, I totally didn't notice there were comments on this thing.

Well, if you keep it in a room which is already full of water, then you basically need an airlock and scuba gear to deal with the thing at all. If you keep it outside, there is no need for an airlock and no danger of flooding, so the scientists can just open or close the side door as necessary to turn the water on or off.
Actually, why don't they just weld the end doors shut… there's a good afternoon project for someone at site 19.

this SCP has pretty good prank potential. "Hey, Frank, could you grab that box in there?" "Sure." *CLANK* *BLOOOOSH* "AIEEEEEE!"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Neat. I like the concept, but a few of the things you say in the article could mesh a little better. To begin with you say that the item can be stored anywhere outside with no problem. Later you say that if both doors are opened, then water will continue to flow out until an equal pressure situation is reached outside. Seems to me that the safest way to store this SCP would be in a sealed room that is already filled with water. That way one or both of the doors can be opened at any time, and because the outside room is already pressurized they can be closed again easily.

Maybe I'm just thinking it through too hard. Good SCP though.
